clue.text: Way out of a regressive state

indicators.note: the solution is taken out of the letters of the following words, so of marks a run within them

explanation.surface: Someone seeks an escape from a backward-looking condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' signals that the answer sits inside 'a regressive'; 'state' is just a link to round off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out, and egress is the formal word for such an exit.

definitions.meaning: ... a worker means hiring or taking them on
an ... manner is a pleasing, attractive one

explanation.surface: A remark that recruiting staff is a delightful business.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: hiring staff, and having an attractive, winning manner.

clue.text: Help one in need-take over his duties

definitions.meaning: to ease or assist someone in distress
to stand in for a sentry or worker at the end of a shift

explanation.surface: Advice to assist a struggling colleague by doing their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed hyphen in 'need-take' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both aiding a sufferer and replacing someone on duty, as a guard is replaced.

clue.text: The lady shortly will have cod perhaps or oysters possibly

parts.note: she will, shortened, gives the contraction she'll
cod is an example of a fish

explanation.surface: A woman will order either cod or oysters for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cod perhaps' looks like part of the menu but supplies FISH; the definition is by example, signalled by 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are an example of molluscs eaten as seafood with hard casings.

clue.text: One produces works that others may play

definitions.text: One produces works that others may play

parts.words: One produces works that others may play
parts.note: reads like a factory boss or a playwright, but the works are pieces of music performed by musicians

explanation.surface: A creator of plays or games that other people perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of music creates scores that orchestras and performers then perform.

parts.note: common means ordinary, plain, of no rank
an old salt is a sailor, so salt means seaman

explanation.surface: A question about plain sodium chloride.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt is old slang for a sailor; the lowest rank of naval rating is the reading here.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior naval rating is a plain sailor, an old salt of no special rank.

explanation.surface: A claim that a small amount of the French language counts for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for small, also used in English for something minor or trifling.

clue.text: Many on course first find a slight trace

indicators.note: the word course is placed at the front, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: soup is a course of a meal
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lots of people on a golf course discover a faint mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests golf or racing but is a meal course; 'first' puts it ahead of C (Roman 100) and ON. 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a tiny amount, a mere hint or touch of something.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a side is a team, such as a football or cricket eleven

explanation.surface: A football team stays behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell or stay in a place, so it can mean remain.

parts.note: to advance is to progress or move forward
an account is a report or description

explanation.surface: Asking about an early payment given to a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' suggests money paid ahead, but here it means forward movement in learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A school document describing how a pupil is getting on and improving.

parts.note: golden is a shade of yellow
a rod is a stick or cane

explanation.surface: A plant growing on a yellow garden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall perennial with sprays of yellow flowers, a common garden flower.

clue.text: Tie up a bundle of straw

definitions.meaning: to bind tightly, as a cook does a chicken
a bale or bound bundle of hay or straw

explanation.surface: Instructions to bind a sheaf of straw.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bind; the noun is a bound bundle of hay or straw.

clue.text: Dreary old convict gets the goose

parts.note: grey means dull or dreary
an old lag is a long-serving prisoner

explanation.surface: A gloomy former prisoner is given the bird for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict, usually 'old lag'.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a species of wild grey goose, ancestor of farmyard geese.

definitions.meaning: a cake with no icing on top is ...

explanation.surface: Someone saw an undecorated sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is read as two words, NOT ICED, describing a cake without icing.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen or observed, and, split in two, describing a bare cake without sugar topping.

indicators.note: the answer creeps into the run of letters spanning the two words before it

explanation.surface: An Italian city has been penetrated by secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moles' looks like spies, but it means skin blemishes, the plural of a Latin word for birthmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Birthmarks and pigmented skin spots are called naevi in medicine.

clue.text: Drum or trumpet perhaps making an electrical connection?

parts.note: an eardrum or an ear trumpet is an ear thing, something to do with hearing
an eardrum or an ear trumpet is an ear thing, something to do with hearing

explanation.surface: A musical instrument being used to wire up a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Drum and trumpet suggest instruments, but they are the eardrum and ear trumpet, each an 'ear thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounding a circuit to the earth for safety is the British term for this wiring step.

parts.note: a miner wears a lamp on the head; a car carries lamps at its front

explanation.surface: A pit worker's lamp fitted to a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner's lamp is worn on the forehead, and a car's front beam lamp bears the same name.

clue.text: Price Ted arranged when it was dilapidated

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Ted sorted out the price on something run-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges PRICE TED; 'when it was' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out by age or neglect, ruined and run-down.

indicators.note: a ship turning over is upset, so its letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An identical vessel overturning under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' rearranges SAME SHIP; 'under' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress laid on a word or point gives it importance, prominence.

parts.note: pink is a mild shade of red
pink is a mild shade of red

explanation.surface: A woman dressed in pink.
explanation.walkthrough: Pink is read as 'mild red', which run together give a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a woman's given name.

indicators.note: the letter goes into the word for a fit

parts.note: an ague is a fit of fever or shivering

explanation.surface: A suitable time to start a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to dispute or have a row.

clue.text: Series of steps got a vet confused

indicators.note: the words are mixed up, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A muddled animal doctor tried to follow a dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges GOT A VET.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French dance made of set steps.

clue.text: The Spanish coil strangely going round has some ringed spots of colour

indicators.note: the shuffled coil surrounds the Spanish article
the letters of coil are arranged in an odd new order

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish spiral twisting round some coloured rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coil' looks like a spiral in the surface; it is only fodder, and 'has some' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelli are eye-like marks, as on a peacock's tail or a butterfly's wing.

clue.text: Engineer processed steel for the keyboard instrument

parts.note: CE stands for civil engineer

indicators.note: steel is processed, so its letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: An engineer worked metal for a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges STEEL into LESTE; 'for the' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The celeste is a small keyed instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, heard in the Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

clue.text: Thus to be embraced by one who is indifferent to pain

definitions.text: one who is indifferent to pain

indicators.note: the small word is held within the word for thus

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A note that being hugged leaves one unmoved by suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic endures hardship without complaint, as the Greek philosophers taught.

definitions.meaning: finished, ended, as in the game is over

explanation.surface: It is finished, all around.
explanation.definitionFit: Means throughout, and also means finished, as a match ending.

parts.note: reads like industrial action, but the movement is a section of a symphony played slowly

explanation.surface: A question about a labour protest working slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: A go-slow is a British form of industrial protest; here the movement is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a direction for a broad, slow tempo, and a movement in that tempo.

indicators.note: the letters of the word are put in a haphazard order

explanation.surface: A butterfly flitting about haphazardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at random' rearranges OPERATING.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a white butterfly whose male has orange wingtips.

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Displaying India and other countries in a new light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges INDIA ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or reveal.

parts.note: taken as written
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A witness testifying at a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture; 'the' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify formally.
